title: LSTM-Based Consumer Behavior Prediction Model Research
venue: 2025 2nd International Conference on Digital Economy and Computer Science (DECS 2025)
tldr: Proposes a bidirectional LSTM with self-attention for consumer purchase prediction, achieving 94.2% accuracy on 80M interaction records from 500K users.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional consumer behavior models (linear regression, decision trees, SVM) cannot capture temporal dependencies in large-scale e-commerce data. Existing deep learning methods lack optimized architectures for multi-class purchase intention prediction.
approach: Constructs a 128-dimensional feature dataset from 500K users and 80M interaction records across clothing, electronics, and home goods.
Uses Apache Spark distributed computing for preprocessing with 30-day sliding windows and 50% overlap.
Implements a bidirectional LSTM with 512 hidden units, self-attention mechanism (8 heads, 64-dim key-value pairs), and adaptive dropout (0.5 to 0.3).
Optimizes via Adam with cosine annealing learning rate scheduling, weighted cross-entropy loss, and L2 regularization.
Evaluates with accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and 10-fold cross-validation with statistical significance testing.
findings: num: Model achieved 94.2% accuracy, 93.8% precision, 94.7% recall, and 94.2% F1-score.
num: 3.0 percentage point improvement over standard LSTM, 10.7 points over traditional ML methods.
num: High-frequency users achieved 96.1% accuracy; new users achieved 91.8% accuracy (23.6% improvement over traditional methods).
Behavioral features dominated (cumulative score 0.521), with purchase frequency the top predictor (0.187).
Removing any Top-5 feature caused a 3.2 percentage point performance decrease.
key_figures_tables: Table 2: Model Performance Comparison → Proposed LSTM at 94.2% vs logistic regression at 78.2%.
Table 3: Performance Analysis by User Groups → Consistent gains across all user segments.
Table 4: Feature Importance Ranking → Purchase frequency (0.187) is the top predictor.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper presents a bidirectional LSTM architecture with self-attention mechanisms for multi-class consumer purchase intention prediction. It demonstrates that behavioral features (purchase frequency, browsing duration) are substantially more predictive than demographic features for e-commerce behavior forecasting. The architecture achieves 94.2% accuracy on a large-scale dataset and shows strong generalization across user segments including new users and high-value customers.
directly_justifies: Behavioral features dominate demographic features (cumulative 0.521 vs 0.078).
BiLSTM with self-attention achieves 94.2% accuracy on 500K user dataset.
limits: Dataset from a single e-commerce platform limits generalizability.
Does not address cold-start for users with no history.
Model has 2.1M parameters requiring GPU for training.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 topic domains was conducted. Topics 6.A and 6.B were flagged as high relevance because the paper's core contribution is predictive modeling of consumer purchase behavior using a time-series forecasting algorithm (LSTM). Topic 3.A was rated low because while the model predicts purchase categories, it does not propose an expense categorization framework. All Philippine-specific topics (1.x, 2.x) were rejected as the paper uses Chinese e-commerce data. Topics 4.x, 5.x, 7.x-14.x were rejected as they address personal finance system design, budgeting, and user experience, which this paper does not cover.

limitations: Model needs improvement for impulsive purchasing and external event-driven consumption.
Single e-commerce platform data may limit generalizability.
remember_this: BiLSTM with attention achieved 94.2% accuracy on 80M interaction records.
Behavioral features are 6.7x more predictive than demographic features.
Self-attention mechanism improved key feature identification by 12.5%.
New users achieved 91.8% accuracy using short-term behavioral features.
